newsitem.title: USA: US, Japan to aim for December insurance deal - Kubo.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan to aim for December insurance deal - Kubo.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Tuesday that Japan and the United States will aim to reach an agreement on their bilateral insurance issue by December 15.

"Ms (U.S. Trade Representative Charlene) Barshefsky and I held negotiations on September 29 and 30. We have agreed to commit to continue talks for a final agreement by December 15, 1996," Kubo told reporters in Washington.
"Since we have reached an agreement like this, there is no possibility of the United States applying the Super 301 (trade clause) over the insurance issue," Kubo said.

The Japanese government said earlier on Tuesday that it would delay until the end of December a go-ahead for newly established subsidiaries of major Japanese insurance firms to issue products in the so-called "third-sector" niche insurance market. This sector covers such areas like personal accident, sickness and nursing care, the stronghold of foreign insurers.
The government's decision was designed to ease tension with the United States over a long-simmering bilateral dispute as to how to open up Japan's $382 billion insurance market.
Kubo said that if the two nations could not reach an agreement on the insurance issue by December 15, Japan could delay domestic insurers' entry into the third sector until after January 1, 1997.
However, he added that such a delay would require the agreement of both Japan and the United States.
